name: CANDEO HOTELS Osaka The Tower
detail: The room was spacious and clean, and I requested a high floor, which I got as I hoped. I used the spa, but even around midnight there were no available lockers, and there were many users, so I returned to my room and came back an hour later. I still think there were more than ten users. Aside from the fact that there was a mountain of bath towels, the location of the outdoor hot spring was excellent, and the washing area was clean. Breakfast was also busy, but there were plenty of tables to sit at, and the food was delicious. The staff provided excellent service as well. I had a very comfortable stay, so I will use it again.

name: APA HOTEL＆RESORT OSAKA NAMBA EKIMAE TOWER
detail: The location was really good. The airport bus stop was on the second floor of the building right next door, so it was nice not to have to walk much with my luggage. (Especially since I was traveling with my parents and child.) We also walked to Dotonbori and Shinsaibashi. The accommodation was very clean and great for relaxing after sightseeing. The check-in and luggage storage process was well organized and convenient. It’s really a value-for-money hotel. I would definitely consider visiting again.

name: Acro Capsule Hotel Namba Dotonbori
detail: As a solo traveler visiting Osaka, there are indeed many options for suitable accommodations in the city center. However, this accommodation, Acro, stands out: 1. Excellent location: Just a few steps out the door and you can reach central attractions like Dotonbori and Shinsaibashi. There are many restaurants around to choose from, and you can also shop in one place, making the location extremely convenient. 2. Affordable price: I stayed right before the Mid-Autumn Festival, and the nightly rate was only a few dozen RMB, which is a great value for a hotel in such a central area. 3. Clean and tidy: Although located in the center, the ceiling height is appropriate and it's not noisy. The clean and tidy environment provides a very good resting space for solo travelers after a day of sightseeing. 4. Excellent service: Upon arriving in Osaka, you can first store your luggage at the front desk and retrieve it at check-in. The attitude of the front desk staff is excellent, and I really appreciate their professionalism. In summary: This is a heartfelt recommendation after my stay. Next time I visit Osaka for a solo trip, I will very likely choose to stay at Acro again~✨

name: APA Hotel and Resort Midosuji Hommachi Ekimae Tower
detail: Overall, I am very satisfied with my stay at the APA Hotel in Osaka, and it is the type of choice I would prioritize for my next visit. The location is very convenient, making travel easy without much thought, whether going to attractions, shopping, or transferring between trains. The check-in and check-out processes are smooth and efficient, so there's hardly any time wasted in lines. The room is overall clean and tidy; although not large, the layout is reasonable and it has everything needed, making it user-friendly. The bedding is quite comfortable, allowing for restful sleep at night; the soundproofing and privacy are also within acceptable ranges, with no significant disturbances. The bathroom and shower area are well maintained, with stable hot water and water pressure, which is a plus for business trips or travel. In terms of service, it feels standardized yet effective, and communication is smooth in case of any issues. Overall, it offers great value for money and is suitable for those who want a hassle-free experience, prioritize efficiency, and have basic requirements for accommodation quality. I recommend it.

name: APA Hotel & Resort Osaka Umeda Eki Tower
detail: I reserved a place to stay in the Umeda area that is affordable and has a large public bath. The room size was suitable for a solo traveler. At night, there was some noise from the road, so sensitive individuals might prefer an interior room without a view. I traveled to and from Kansai Airport using the Haruka, and although it's a bit far, the road conditions are good, so there were no difficulties in getting around. Depending on the weather, you can move underground and use the elevator near the hotel to go up to ground level, but if it's your first time, finding the way can be challenging. There are various shopping malls about a 15-minute walk away, and it's also easy to get to Namba by subway. There's a Lawson convenience store on the 4th floor of the hotel, which is convenient, and there are several convenience stores and restaurants around. The large public bath can be used until 1 AM, so it seems great for unwinding even after coming back late. The staff is friendly, and the check-in and check-out procedures are simple.

name: APA Hotel Namba-Eki Higashi
detail: It's very convenient to store your luggage before and after check-in, just a 5-minute walk from Nanba Station, and there's a Lawson convenience store and Don Quijote right in front, which is great for shopping. It was also relatively quiet at night, so I could sleep comfortably. The elevator didn't have air conditioning, so it was quite hot, which could be considered a downside. I'm satisfied with everything else.

name: APA Hotel Osaka Higobashi Ekimae Tower
detail: It is just a short walk from Festival Hall, located along the Tosabori River. Although it is not in the center of Umeda, it is a calm place with beautiful night views. It is very convenient as it is directly connected to the exit of Higobashi Station. The large public bath is luxurious and clean, the Wi-Fi connection is solid, and check-in and check-out are prompt. Overall, I was very satisfied; however, there were two things that I found disappointing. The first was that the threshold of the bathroom in the room was too high. They may have made it high on purpose to prevent water from leaking into the room, but I wondered if it really needed to be that high. I was afraid of tripping every time I used the toilet. I think it could be dangerous for elderly people. The second issue was the elevator. When returning to my room after using the large bath on the second floor, the elevator was packed with businessmen, which was very unpleasant. A different business hotel had a women-only elevator, which was great... However, there are only four elevators, and since it is already crowded, I think it would be difficult to improve, but I wanted to mention that it was quite uncomfortable. Additionally, I used to enjoy breakfast at the Vietnamese restaurant on the top floor, but now it has been replaced with a regular breakfast on the second floor, which was disappointing. I would have liked fresh orange juice and other items.

name: APA Hotel Shin-Osaka ekimae
detail: It is close to Shin-Osaka Station and located on the east side of the station, so the surrounding area is relatively quiet, and the location is very good. The hotel is clean and has a more upscale impression compared to a typical business hotel. The room was slightly on the smaller side, but it was sufficient for one person, and I was able to stay comfortably. I was also happy to have a large public bath, which I used twice, once in the evening and once in the morning. It was very nice to relieve the fatigue from my business trip and travel. The breakfast is a bit on the expensive side, but the selection was substantial, and I was satisfied. I would like to use this hotel again when staying around Shin-Osaka Station.

name: Capsule Inn Osaka - Men Only
detail: The location is within the Hankyu Higashidori shopping street, so there are plenty of places to eat and drink nearby. The facilities include a large public bath, an outdoor bath, a pool, and a sauna, and it seems there are also options for body scrubs and massages. Additionally, the staff all seem to work efficiently. One issue I faced was that the building is large, and I often found myself wandering and getting lost when going to the baths. PS. The breakfast is free, and honestly, I didn't expect much, but there was a surprisingly good variety in the buffet. I arrived late at night intending just to sleep, but I was very satisfied.

name: APA Hotel Namba Shinsaibashi Nishi
detail: I couldn't speak Japanese, so I used English, but the staff were very kind and helpful. Since we were family, we used the connecting room, which was small but clean and comfortable. The breakfast wasn't very diverse, but it was neat and delicious. The curry, in particular, was tasty. The location was great, with no issues walking to the shopping district and Dotonbori, and the luggage storage service was especially useful.
